mainTopic: The meaning of the words טריפה and נבלה in the פסוקים about fat and about bird נבלה, and whether the purity of נבלה fat applies to a kosher or a non-kosher animal
overview: The פסוק in ויקרא 7:24 says the fat (חלב) of a נבלה and of a טריפה may be used for any work. This teaches that such fat does not carry נבלה impurity. The גמרא keeps trying to find the job of the word טריפה in that פסוק. First it says the word includes a kosher wild animal (חיה), but that reading is pushed away. Then אביי says the word is needed for its plain meaning, and that answer is also knocked down. In the end רבא explains that the word teaches that the איסור of טריפה, like the איסור of נבלה, takes effect on top of the איסור of חלב. The גמרא then goes back to the bird פסוקים and shows how רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה each use the words טריפה and נבלה, including the rules of a כזית and כדי אכילת פרס. Finally a ברייתא proves that the purity of נבלה fat applies only to a kosher animal. It faces a competing comparison, and its reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rule about non-kosher fat already comes from 'the fat of a נבלה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier use of the word טריפה. The rule that a טמאה's fat is impure already comes from the words 'וחלב נבלה', which only cover fat that is forbidden because of the איסור of eating חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can learn this from 'and the fat of a carcass' too. The פסוק only speaks about fat that is forbidden because of 'do not eat fat'. That leaves out a non-kosher animal's fat, which is forbidden only because the whole animal is טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the earlier reading of the word טריפה. It says that word is not needed for the rule about a טמאה, because 'וחלב נבלה' already teaches it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that makes חלב pure speaks about fat that is forbidden as חלב. A non-kosher animal's fat is not forbidden as חלב at all. It is forbidden only because the animal is טמא. So the פסוק never covered it, and its fat stays impure without any need for the word טריפה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let me derive it instead from... (this source already teaches it)
The forbidden fat of an animal that died without proper שחיטה
A Torah איסור of 'do not eat'
This one is left out
Here: a non-kosher kind of animal

phrases.english: This too,
let me derive it from 'and the fat of a carcass' –
meaning fat whose prohibition is because of
'you shall not eat' the fat of a carcass;
this one is left out, whose prohibition is not
because of 'you shall not eat [the fat of a carcass]',
phrases.notes: Some versions add the words in square brackets here.

phrases.english: but rather because it is a non-kosher animal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier reading that the word טריפה excludes a non-kosher animal.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that uses the word טריפה to teach that a טמאה's fat is impure.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words 'וחלב נבלה' only cover fat forbidden as חלב. A טמאה's fat is forbidden for a different reason, so it is already left out. That makes the word טריפה extra.

steps.title: The word טריפה comes to include a kosher wild animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new job to the word טריפה. It includes the fat of a kosher wild animal (חיה) in the rule of purity, even though that fat is permitted to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the word 'טריפה' is needed to include a wild animal. Otherwise you might say the פסוק only covers an animal whose fat is forbidden and whose meat is permitted. That would leave out a wild animal, whose fat and meat are both permitted. So the word teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by moving the word טריפה to a different job. It now includes a חיה, so that a חיה's נבלה fat is also pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra word, we might think purity only applies to an animal whose fat is treated differently from its meat, like a בהמה. A חיה's fat is permitted just like its meat, so we might have left it out. The word טריפה shows that any animal that can become a טריפה is included.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed (for this teaching)
To include
A wild animal (like a deer), whose fat is permitted to eat
It would have entered your mind to say (the mistaken thought)
So it teaches us (otherwise)

steps.confusionAlert: The fat of a kosher חיה is permitted to eat. Only a בהמה's חלב is forbidden. That is exactly why someone might have thought a חיה is not covered by this פסוק.

phrases.english: Rather, this word 'tereifa'
is needed to include a wild animal –
for it would have entered your mind to say:
the verse covers an animal whose fat is forbidden and whose meat is permitted,
which leaves out this one, whose fat and meat are both permitted;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הַאי טְרֵיפָה מִיבְּעֵי לְאֵיתוֹיֵי חַיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by giving the word טריפה a new purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a new job (including a חיה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only an animal whose fat is forbidden while its meat is permitted is covered, so a חיה would be left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word טריפה includes a חיה. Its נבלה fat is also pure.

steps.title: A wild animal looks just like a non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: Someone objects that a חיה cannot be treated differently from a טמאה. In both, the fat has the same status as the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What makes a non-kosher animal different? That its fat is no different from its meat? A wild animal's fat is also no different from its meat!
steps.whatsHappening: Someone challenges the answer in step 2. If a טמאה is left out because its fat has the same status as its meat, a חיה should be left out for the same reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a טמאה, both fat and meat are forbidden. In a חיה, both fat and meat are permitted. Either way, the fat is not treated differently from the meat. So why should a חיה's fat be pure while a טמאה's fat is impure?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Different, treated separately

phrases.english: He said to him:
What is different about a non-kosher animal?
That its fat is not different from its meat;
a wild animal too –
its fat is not different from its meat!
phrases.notes: In a wild animal, both the fat and the meat are permitted to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the word טריפה includes a חיה while a טמאה stays excluded.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reason that excludes a טמאה (fat has the same status as meat) applies equally to a חיה.

steps.title: A second objection from 'ואכל לא תאכלוהו'
steps.stepSummary: The objector adds a second point. The end of the same פסוק, 'ואכל לא תאכלוהו', seems to speak only about fat that is forbidden to eat, which would leave out a חיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, isn't it written: 'But you shall surely not eat it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The objector brings a second challenge to step 2, this time from the words of the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק ends by saying this fat may not be eaten. A חיה's fat is permitted to eat, so these words suggest the פסוק is not talking about a חיה at all. That makes it hard to say the word טריפה includes a חיה.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore (a second objection)
But isn't it written?
'But you shall surely not eat it' (ויקרא 7:24)

steps.whatToRemember: The word טריפה was first read as excluding a טמאה, then as including a חיה. Now that second reading faces two objections: a חיה looks like a טמאה, and 'ואכל לא תאכלוהו' points to fat that is forbidden to eat.

phrases.english: And furthermore, isn't it written:
'But you shall surely not eat it'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:24. A wild animal's fat may be eaten, so these words seem to leave it out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the answer of step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the word טריפה includes a חיה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק speaks of fat that may not be eaten. A חיה's fat may be eaten, so the פסוק seems to exclude a חיה, not include it.

steps.title: אביי: The word is needed for its plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the word טריפה teaches its own simple law: the fat of a dead טריפה is pure. Without it, we might have compared a טריפה to a טמאה, whose fat is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: the word טריפה is needed for itself. Otherwise you might say: a טמאה is forbidden while alive, and a טריפה is forbidden while alive. So just as a טמאה's fat is impure, a טריפה's fat should be impure too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier answer and brings a new one from אביי. He says the word טריפה is not extra at all, because it teaches its own plain law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמאה and a טריפה share one feature: both are forbidden even while the animal is still alive. That shared feature could lead us to say that a טריפה's fat is impure, just like a טמאה's fat. The Torah writes טריפה to block that comparison and tell us the fat of a טריפה is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for its own plain meaning, not as an extra word for a new teaching
Forbidden even while the animal is still alive
So that you should not say (it blocks a mistaken comparison)
Since; it introduces the shared feature behind a comparison

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
The word tereifa is needed for its own sake;
so that you should not say:
since a non-kosher animal is forbidden while alive,
and a tereifa is forbidden while alive,
just as a non-kosher animal's fat is impure,
so too a tereifa's fat would be impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: טְרֵיפָה לְגוּפֵיהּ אִיצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the earlier explanation of the word טריפה, which was challenged in steps 3-4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading: the word is needed for its plain meaning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might compare a טריפה to a טמאה, since both are forbidden while alive, and say its fat is impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word טריפה teaches that the fat of a dead טריפה is pure.

steps.title: By that logic, the bird verse's word would also be needed
steps.stepSummary: If we worry about comparisons like this, then the word טריפה in the bird פסוק would also be needed for its plain meaning. Otherwise we might compare a טריפה bird to a non-kosher bird and say it does not make things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this word is also needed for itself. Otherwise you might say: a non-kosher bird is forbidden to eat, and a טריפה is forbidden to eat. So just as a non-kosher bird does not make things impure, a טריפה should not make things impure either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי. If his kind of reasoning is correct, then the word טריפה in the פסוק about birds would also be used up for its plain meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claims the Torah has to block a mistaken comparison between a טריפה and a טמאה. Then the same kind of comparison is possible with birds: a non-kosher bird does not make things impure, so we might think a טריפה bird does not either. That word would then be needed just to block that mistake, and it could not be used for the other teaching it is used for elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if we accept your reasoning
This one is also needed (for its plain meaning)
A non-kosher bird
Does not make things impure

phrases.english: If so,
this word is also needed for itself;
phrases.notes: "This word" is טריפה in the פסוק about eating a dead bird, ויקרא 17:15.

phrases.english: so that you should not say:
since a non-kosher bird is forbidden to eat,
and a tereifa is forbidden to eat,
just as a non-kosher bird does not make things impure,
so too a tereifa should not make things impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's reasoning by showing it would also apply to the bird פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the word טריפה is needed to block a comparison to a טמאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If such comparisons need to be blocked, the bird פסוק's word טריפה would also be used up for its plain meaning. That undermines the way the word is used elsewhere.

steps.title: A טריפה cannot be compared to a non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: A second attack on אביי: the comparison he worries about could never be made. A טמאה was never kosher, but a טריפה had a time when it was kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, can we really learn a טריפה from a טמאה? A טמאה never had a time when it was fit, but a טריפה did have a time when it was fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second problem for אביי. Nobody would make his comparison in the first place, so there is nothing for the word to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole answer depends on the risk that we would compare a טריפה to a טמאה. But the two are very different: a טמאה was never kosher, while a טריפה was a kosher animal before it became damaged. Since the comparison fails anyway, the Torah would not need a word to stop it.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; it adds a second objection
Is it really possible to learn (one case from another)?
A time when it was fit or kosher

phrases.english: And furthermore,
can we really learn a tereifa from a non-kosher animal?!

phrases.aramaic: טְמֵאָה לֹא הָיְתָה לָהּ שְׁעַת הַכּוֹשֶׁר,
phrases.english: A non-kosher animal never had a time when it was fit,
but a tereifa did have a time when it was fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, מִי אִיכָּא לְמֵילַף טְרֵפָה מִטְּמֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, independent objection to אביי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between a טריפה and a טמאה that אביי says the word blocks
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison could never be made, because a טריפה once had a kosher status and a טמאה never did. So no word is needed to block it.

steps.title: Even a טריפה from birth belongs to a kosher species
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא imagines a defense: an animal that was a טריפה from birth was never kosher. It rejects this, because that animal still belongs to a kosher species.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: what about an animal that was a טריפה from the womb? At least its species is kosher!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone defending אביי with the case of an animal born as a טריפה, and quickly pushes that defense away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal that was a טריפה from birth never had a kosher moment, so it might seem to match a טמאה. But it still comes from a kosher species, and a טמאה does not. So the difference remains, and the objection from step 7 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; it introduces a possible defense
An animal that was a טריפה from the womb, from birth
At least in its species there is (kosher status)

phrases.english: And if you will say:
what can be said about a tereifa from the womb?
At least its species has kosher status!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: טְרֵיפָה מִבֶּטֶן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a possible defense against step 7's objection, so that objection holds.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested defense that an animal born a טריפה matches a טמאה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Even an animal born a טריפה belongs to a kosher species, which a טמאה does not.

steps.title: רבא: The איסור of טריפה takes effect on top of the איסור of חלב
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation. Just as the איסור of נבלה takes effect on the איסור of חלב, the word טריפה teaches that the איסור of טריפה also takes effect on the איסור of חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: the Torah said, let the איסור of נבלה come and take effect on the איסור of חלב. Let the איסור of טריפה come and take effect on the איסור of חלב.
steps.whatsHappening: After אביי's answer falls, the גמרא brings רבא's new answer. In his reading, these words teach a law about eating rather than about purity: a second איסור lands on top of the איסור of חלב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one might think that once fat is already forbidden as חלב, a new איסור cannot be added to it. רבא says the Torah teaches that the איסור of נבלה, and also the איסור of טריפה, does take effect on it. So someone who eats חלב from a נבלה or a טריפה breaks two prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: Let a prohibition come and take effect (on top of another one)
The prohibition of eating an animal that died without proper שחיטה
The prohibition of eating forbidden fat
The Torah said; this is how רבא reads the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: אביי's reading (that the word טריפה teaches the fat is pure) was rejected. רבא reads the פסוק as teaching that the איסור of נבלה and the איסור of טריפה each take effect on top of the איסור of חלב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a key idea: the Torah can make one איסור take effect on something that is already forbidden, so one act of eating can carry two prohibitions.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said,
the Torah said:
let the prohibition of a carcass come
and take effect on the prohibition of forbidden fat,
let the prohibition of a tereifa come
and take effect on the prohibition of forbidden fat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא, הַתּוֹרָה אָמְרָה: יָבֹא אִיסּוּר נְבֵילָה וְיָחוּל עַל אִיסּוּר חֵלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected answer with a new reading of the word טריפה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the פסוק: it teaches a prohibition taking effect on another prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The איסור of חלב might block any later איסור from taking effect on the same fat.
steps.terutzMaskana: The איסור of נבלה and the איסור of טריפה both take effect on the איסור of חלב, so eating such fat breaks two prohibitions.

steps.title: Why both נבלה and טריפה are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the פסוק must mention both נבלה and טריפה, because each has a special feature that might make its law unique.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both words are needed. If the פסוק had told us only about נבלה, I would say the איסור takes effect on חלב only because a נבלה makes things impure, but not a טריפה. If it had told us only about טריפה, I would say it works only because a טריפה is forbidden while still alive, but not a נבלה. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question about רבא's teaching. If נבלה and טריפה teach the same rule, why does the פסוק need both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלה is stronger in one way: it makes things impure. A טריפה is stronger in a different way: its איסור starts while the animal is still alive. Since each has its own strength, we could not learn either one from the other, so the פסוק writes both.

keyTerms.meaning: They are needed: both teachings are necessary, and one cannot be learned from the other
It taught us
Because it makes things impure
Its prohibition starts while it is still alive
I would say no (this rule does not apply)

steps.whatToRemember: A צריכותא shows that each case has its own special feature, so the תורה must write both.

phrases.english: And both are needed;
phrases.notes: Both words in רבא's פסוק from step 9: חלב נבלה and חלב טריפה.

phrases.english: for if it had taught us only a נבלה,
I would say that is because it makes things impure,
but a טריפה, I would say no;
and if it had taught us only a טריפה,
I would say that is because its prohibition starts while it is alive,
but a נבלה, I would say no;
so both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבא's explanation by showing that neither word in the פסוק is extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own special feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only one word, I would limit the rule to that case because of its special feature.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both words are needed, so the rule applies to both נבלה and טריפה.

steps.title: What does רבי מאיר learn from the word טריפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with the word טריפה in the bird פסוק, since he does not use it the way רבי יהודה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what does he do with this word "טריפה"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves back to the bird פסוק. It asks how רבי מאיר uses the word טריפה, and its answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used this word to teach that a slaughtered טריפה bird makes things impure. רבי מאיר says it does not, so the word seems to have no job for him. The גמרא wants to know what he learns from it.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (How does he use this word?)

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר,
what does he do with this word "טריפה"?
phrases.notes: This is the word טריפה in the bird פסוק, which רבי יהודה used for a slaughtered טריפה bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הַאי ״טְרֵפָה״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חלב discussion and returns to how each תנא reads the bird פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which law רבי מאיר learns from the word טריפה in the bird פסוק.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: excluding a bird slaughtered inside the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses the word טריפה to teach that a regular bird slaughtered inside the עזרה is excluded. It does not make things impure like a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it to exclude a slaughtering done inside the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. רבי מאיר uses the word to exclude a regular bird that was slaughtered inside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חולין bird slaughtered inside the עזרה may not be eaten. One might think that makes it like a נבלה, so it would make things impure. The word טריפה teaches that it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different teaching)
To exclude
A slaughtering done inside the עזרה

phrases.english: He needs it
to exclude a slaughtering that is done inside.
phrases.notes: "Inside" means inside the עזרה. It's talking about a regular bird, not קדשים.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא לִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר uses טריפה to exclude a bird slaughtered inside the עזרה from making things impure.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns it from a second טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the law of a bird slaughtered inside the עזרה from a second place where the word טריפה is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? Another "טריפה" is written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה knows the law about a bird slaughtered inside the עזרה, since he already used the first טריפה for something else. It answers that the word טריפה appears a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used the first טריפה to teach that a slaughtered טריפה bird makes things impure. He learns the law about a bird slaughtered inside the עזרה from the second טריפה. So he gets both laws.

keyTerms.meaning: Another (a second one)
It is written (in a פסוק)

phrases.english: And רבי יהודה, how does he learn this?
Another "טריפה" is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks that רבי יהודה also has a source for the law that רבי מאיר learned in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second mention of טריפה gives רבי יהודה the law about a bird slaughtered inside the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי מאיר uses both mentions of טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר uses one טריפה to exclude a bird slaughtered inside the עזרה, and the other to teach that a non-kosher bird does not make things impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר? One is to exclude a slaughtering done inside the עזרה, and one is to exclude a non-kosher bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with the second טריפה. It answers that he uses it to exclude a non-kosher bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each תנא uses each word for one law, so neither word is extra. רבי יהודה uses the words for the טריפה bird and for the bird slaughtered inside the עזרה. רבי מאיר uses them for the bird slaughtered inside the עזרה and for the non-kosher bird, whose dead body does not make things impure.

keyTerms.meaning: One is for this, and one is for that
A non-kosher bird

steps.whatToRemember: Both תנאים use both mentions of טריפה. They only disagree about which laws the words teach.

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר, what does he do with the second one?
One is to exclude a slaughtering that is done inside,
and one is to exclude a non-kosher bird.
phrases.notes: He means the dead body of a non-kosher bird does not make things impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר – חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי שְׁחִיטָה שֶׁהִיא לִפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the comparison by showing that רבי מאיר also has a use for the second טריפה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second טריפה teaches רבי מאיר that a non-kosher bird does not make things impure.

steps.title: רבי יהודה learns the non-kosher bird law from the word נבלה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns that a non-kosher bird does not make things impure from the word נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה learns it from the word 'נבלה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains where רבי יהודה learns that a non-kosher bird does not make things impure. He learns it from the word נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר learned this law from the extra word טריפה. רבי יהודה already used both words טריפה for other laws, so he needs a different source. He finds it in the word נבלה: only a bird that is forbidden because it is a נבלה makes things impure. A non-kosher bird is forbidden for a different reason, so it is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal or bird that died without a proper שחיטה
He learns it out (from)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda –
phrases.notes: The question is: where does he learn that a non-kosher bird does not make things impure? That was רבי מאיר's teaching in the last step.

phrases.english: he derives it from "carcass."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 14 said רבי מאיר learns the non-kosher bird law from טריפה. This step gives רבי יהודה's source for the same law.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where does רבי יהודה learn that a non-kosher bird does not make things impure?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the word נבלה in the פסוק.

steps.title: What רבי מאיר does with the word נבלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר learns from נבלה and answers that it teaches the amount of a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, what does he do with this word 'נבלה'? He uses it to teach that the amount of eating is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר learns from the word נבלה, since he does not use it for the non-kosher bird law. It answers that he uses it to teach that you must eat a כזית to become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word in the פסוק must teach something. רבי מאיר used טריפה for the non-kosher bird, so נבלה is free. He uses it to set the minimum amount: eating less than a כזית of a bird נבלה does not make a person impure.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (What does he learn from it?)
The amount of eating that counts
The size of an olive, the standard amount for eating in the Torah

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir –
what does he do with this word "carcass"?
It teaches that the amount of eating is an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר הַאי נְבֵלָה מַאי עָבֵיד לֵהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי יהודה's use of נבלה, the גמרא asks what רבי מאיר does with that same word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי מאיר learn from the word נבלה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It teaches that the amount you must eat to become impure is a כזית.

steps.title: The first פסוק already speaks about eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: why do we need נבלה for the כזית rule, when the first פסוק already uses the language of eating?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him learn it from the first פסוק, since the Torah wrote it using the language of eating!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי מאיר's answer. The amount of a כזית could already be learned from the first פסוק, which speaks about eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק (ויקרא 17:15) says 'every person who eats a נבלה.' Whenever the Torah speaks about eating, the amount is a כזית. So the extra word נבלה seems unneeded for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: But let me learn it from
The first פסוק
The language of eating
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah or ה׳

phrases.english: But let me derive it from the first verse,
since the Merciful One expressed it in the language of eating!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 16 by saying the כזית rule is already known from another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's use of נבלה to teach the כזית amount.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first פסוק already uses eating language, which already means a כזית, so the word נבלה would be extra.

steps.title: One teaches the amount, the other teaches the time limit
steps.stepSummary: Both are needed: one teaches the amount of a כזית, the other teaches it must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: One teaches the amount of eating, a כזית, and one teaches the time for eating, within the time it takes to eat half a loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both sources are needed because each teaches a different rule about eating. One teaches how much (a כזית) and the other teaches how fast (within כדי אכילת פרס).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating has two measures: the amount and the time. Eating a כזית slowly over a long time does not count as one act of eating. So one source teaches the כזית, and the other teaches that the כזית must be eaten within כדי אכילת פרס to make a person impure.

keyTerms.meaning: One (of the two sources)
The time it takes to eat half a loaf of bread
Half a loaf

steps.whatToRemember: For a bird נבלה to make a person impure, he must eat a כזית, and he must eat it within כדי אכילת פרס. רבי מאיר learns one rule from each of the two sources.
steps.confusionAlert: The second שיעור is not a second amount of food. It is a time limit: how quickly the כזית must be eaten.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a general rule in הלכה: eating is measured both by amount (כזית) and by time (כדי אכילת פרס).

phrases.english: One teaches that the amount of eating is an olive-bulk,
and one teaches that the measure of eating
phrases.notes: Here the measure is about time, not about how much food.

phrases.english: is within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְשִׁיעוּר אֲכִילָה בִּכְזַיִת וְחַד לְשִׁיעוּר אֲכִילָה בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17 by giving each source its own rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source teaches a separate rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first פסוק's eating language already teaches the כזית, so נבלה is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: One source teaches the כזית amount and the other teaches the time limit of כדי אכילת פרס, so both are needed.

steps.title: Why the time limit had to be taught
steps.stepSummary: Without the extra teaching, we might think that since bird נבלה impurity is unusual, eating it even more slowly than כדי אכילת פרס would still make a person impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: since this impurity is a חידוש, a person should become impure even if he ate it over more than כדי אכילת פרס. So the Torah teaches us that this is not true.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 18. It explains why we need a source for the כדי אכילת פרס time limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bird נבלה makes a person impure only by eating it, not by touching or carrying it, so it is a חידוש. Since it is so unusual, we might have thought it has no normal time limit. The extra word in the פסוק tells us the normal limit of כדי אכילת פרס still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the first wrong idea)
A new, unusual law that does not follow normal logic
The time it takes to eat half a loaf. Eating a כזית within this time counts as one act of eating.
It teaches us (the real answer)

steps.whatToRemember: Bird נבלה makes a person impure only if he eats a כזית, and only if he eats it within כדי אכילת פרס.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that being a חידוש makes this law weaker. The worry was the opposite: that a חידוש might be stricter and have no time limit.

phrases.english: It would enter your mind to say:
since it is a novelty,
phrases.notes: The novelty is that this impurity comes from eating, not from touching or carrying.

phrases.english: even more than the time it takes to eat a half-loaf
he should also become impure;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 18 by explaining why the time-limit teaching was needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows why a second source is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since bird נבלה impurity is a חידוש, eating it even over more than כדי אכילת פרס would still make a person impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The normal limit of כדי אכילת פרס applies to bird נבלה too.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the verse about fat speaks of a kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the פסוק 'the fat of a נבלה and the fat of a טריפה' is talking about the fat of a kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And the fat of a נבלה and the fat of a טריפה': the פסוק is speaking about the fat of a kosher animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by bringing a ברייתא. The ברייתא states which kind of animal a certain פסוק about fat is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the fat of a נבלה or טריפה may be used for any work, and this teaches that such fat does not carry נבלה impurity. The ברייתא says this pure status is said only about a kosher animal. The next steps will question and prove this.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden fat of an animal
A kosher animal
The פסוק is speaking about

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And the fat of a carcass and the fat of a tereifa":
about the fat of a kosher animal
the verse is speaking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the impurity of fat, after the discussion of bird נבלה ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק about the fat of a נבלה and טריפה refers to the fat of a kosher animal.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means a non-kosher animal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: how do we know the פסוק is about a kosher animal? Maybe it is about a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say the פסוק is speaking about the fat of a kosher animal. Or maybe it is only speaking about the fat of a non-kosher animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own statement. It is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself does not say which animal it means. So the ברייתא raises the other possibility, that it means a non-kosher animal, and now it has to show why that reading is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opens a question about the claim just made)
Or perhaps it is only (suggests the other possibility)
A non-kosher animal

phrases.english: You say
the verse is speaking about the fat of a kosher animal;
or perhaps it is only
about the fat of a non-kosher animal?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּחֵלֶב בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the claim of step 20 by offering the opposite reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why should the פסוק be read as talking about a kosher animal and not a non-kosher one?

steps.title: Proof by comparing fat to שחיטה
steps.stepSummary: The Torah makes an animal pure through שחיטה only when it is kosher. In the same way, it makes fat pure only when it comes from a kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can answer: the Torah made an animal pure because it was slaughtered, and it made fat pure because it is fat. Just as שחיטה makes only a kosher animal pure and not a non-kosher one, so too fat is pure only in a kosher animal and not in a non-kosher one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its question. It compares two cases where the Torah makes something pure and shows that both apply only to kosher animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שחיטה stops a kosher animal from becoming a נבלה, but a non-kosher animal is impure even after שחיטה. The fat rule is the same kind of law, since it also takes something out of נבלה impurity. So it also applies only to a kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: You can say (introduces the answer)
Made pure
Because it was slaughtered
Just as ... so too (a comparison)

steps.whatToRemember: The fat of a נבלה is pure only in a kosher animal. This is learned from שחיטה, which also makes only a kosher animal pure.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the fat of a non-kosher animal is pure. The ברייתא's point is that this pure status is only for a kosher animal.

phrases.english: You can say:
He made it pure because it was slaughtered,
and He made it pure because it is fat;
just as when He made it pure because it was slaughtered,
it is about a kosher animal and not a non-kosher one,
so too when He made it pure because it is fat,
it is about a kosher animal and not a non-kosher one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 and confirms the claim of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Comparing to שחיטה, which makes only a kosher animal pure, shows that the fat rule also applies only to a kosher animal.

steps.title: Maybe fat should be compared to a non-kosher case instead
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא offers a different comparison. When the Torah removed something from the category of נבלה, it did so for a non-kosher animal. So when it removes fat from נבלה impurity, maybe that also applies only to a non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe go this way: The Torah made something pure, taking it out of the category of נבלה. It also made fat pure because it is fat. Just as taking something out of נבלה impurity applies to a non-kosher animal and not a kosher one, so too making fat pure should apply to a non-kosher animal and not a kosher one!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the proof from step 22. It suggests a different comparison that points to the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, fat was compared to שחיטה, which works only on a kosher animal. Here the ברייתא says fat could just as easily be compared to a case where the Torah removed נבלה impurity only from a non-kosher animal. If that comparison is the right one, the פסוק about pure fat would be talking about a non-kosher animal.

keyTerms.meaning: Or go this way, a phrase that offers a competing line of reasoning
He (the Torah) made pure
From the category of
With a non-kosher animal
With a kosher animal

steps.confusionAlert: Here טמאה and טהורה mean non-kosher and kosher animals. They do not mean ritually impure and ritually pure, even though the same sentence is talking about making things pure.

phrases.english: Or go this way:
phrases.notes: Literally 'go yourself to this path.' It's a way of saying 'maybe the comparison should run the other way.'

phrases.english: The Torah made pure, taking it out of the category of a carcass,
and it made pure because it is fat;
just as when it made pure, taking it out of the category of a carcass,
it was with a non-kosher animal and not a kosher one,
so too when it made pure because it is fat,
it should be with a non-kosher animal and not a kosher one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It challenges the comparison in step 22 by offering a competing comparison with the opposite result.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof in step 22 that the purity of fat applies only to a kosher animal because it is compared to שחיטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is an equally good comparison to the removal of נבלה impurity, which applies only to a non-kosher animal. That comparison would lead to the opposite conclusion.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins its reply
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא opens its answer to the competing comparison with the words 'You may say.' The actual reply comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may say:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. The ברייתא is about to explain why the comparison to שחיטה is the better one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'You may say' tell us an answer to the challenge in step 23 is coming. The content of the answer continues in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: You may say, a phrase that introduces a reply

phrases.english: You may say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It opens the response to the competing comparison raised in step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setup for a reply that decides which comparison is stronger (the reply continues afterward).
